proxy_language: Proto-Tupi (with Proto-Tupi-Guarani as a secondary, shallower layer); alternatively Proto-Tucanoan or Proto-Carib as equally unverifiable options
proxy_rationale: Pedra Pintada (Monte Alegre, Para, Brazil; c. 11,200-10,000 BP, Roosevelt et al. 1996) is a Pleistocene/early Holocene rock-shelter culture with no linguistic remains. No language can be attributed to it. Proto-Tupi (homeland probably in southwestern Amazonia, Rondonia/Madeira region; Rodrigues 1958, Rodrigues and Cabral 2012) is the best-documented Amazonian reconstruction near the Lower Amazon, but Tupian expansion is much later than 10,000 BP, so the link is purely a regional-flavor choice. Carib (north bank, Guiana Shield) and Tucanoan are equally defensible. Names should sound plausibly Amazonian, not be presented as Pedra Pintada speech.
phonology: Proto-Tupi (Rodrigues/Cabral/Jensen, simplified, with Tupi-Guarani-style notation): consonants *p *t *k *kw *ʔ (glottal stop, written ' or ?) *m *n *ŋ (written ng or ñ), *β (written b or w), *r, *s, *ʃ (written x), *h, *j (written y). Vowels: *i *e *a *o *u and the high central unrounded *ɨ (written y or ɨ), plus *ã etc. nasality as a feature spreading across the word. Documented TG forms use p t k kw ' m n ng b/w r s x h y, vowels i e a o u y(ɨ). Many Tupian languages have systematic nasal harmony.
phonotactics: Syllable shape is (C)V; codas are absent or limited in the proto-language (TG daughters rarely add final stops/nasals). No consonant clusters; words alternate consonant and vowel (CVCV...). Words usually end in a vowel; some TG roots end in a glottal stop or short consonant. Stress is typically final or penultimate. Nasal vowels cause adjacent consonants to become nasalized (b>m, r>n). Avoid f, l, q, d, g as standalone proto-phonemes, v, z, c; these are foreign to Tupian.
orthography: Use a simplified Tupi-Guarani Latin transliteration: p t k ' m n ng b r s x h y (for ɨ) w y; vowels a e i o u and y (high central), with ~ or tilde for nasality (ã ẽ ĩ õ ũ). Optional apostrophe for glottal stop. Hyphens separate morphemes in compounds (as in Old Tupi/Nheengatu convention).
morphology: Agglutinative, head-final in nominals. Roots are bound to personal prefixes (a- 1sg, ere- 2sg, o- 3, ja- 1pl, etc. in TG). Old Tupi relational prefixes: r- (contiguous), t- (non-contiguous/absolutive), s- (3rd person) mark nominal possession ('rendaga). Nominal suffixes: -a (nominalizer in Old Tupi), -ra (agent/instrument nominalizer), -sara/-sar (agent, -maker/-er), -pe (locative 'in, at'), -wera (ex-, past), -ete (true, real, intensive), -ran (like, resembling), -ngaba/-aba/-ba (instrument, place or nominalizer), -ita (plural/collective), -ty (place of abundance, as in -tyba). Verbs are inflected for person, no tense in the proto-language.
compounding: Compounds and genitives are head-final: modifier + head (possessor before possessum), e.g. Old Tupi kuarasy 'sun' + oka 'house'. 'X of Y' is simply Y-X with Y as possessor (no linker). 'Y-maker' = Y + root + -sara/-ra. Place names add -pe (in) or -tyba (abundance of, place of). Adjectives (including color terms) follow the noun in Old Tupi and Nheengatu (e.g. i-pira 'fish' + una 'black'); use head-initial for adjectives and head-final for genitives. Reduplication marks plural/intensity (e.g. putir-putir). Use hyphen or space between compounded elements.
noun_phrase_order: Possessor before possessed (genitive precedes head: 'Y X' for 'X of Y'). Qualifying adjectives or stative nouns usually follow the head noun (N-Adj). Numerals/demonstratives precede. Postpositions rather than prepositions.
sources: Rodrigues, A. D. (1958) 'Phonologie historique du Tupi-Guarani' and later Tupi reconstruction articles
Rodrigues, A. D. and Cabral, A. S. A. C. (2012) 'Tupian' in Campbell and Grondona (eds.), The Indigenous Languages of South America
Jensen, C. (1999) 'Tupi-Guarani' in Dixon and Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages
Navarro, E. A. (2013) Metodo moderno de tupi antigo
Roosevelt, A. C. et al. (1996) 'Paleoindian Cave Dwellers in the Amazon: The Peopling of the Americas', Science 272
Glottolog and ASJP entries for Tupian, Cariban, Tucanoan
notes: Pedra Pintada is archaeologically attested only (rock paintings, fishing, tree-fruit gathering). Any proxy language is speculative; names should merely evoke Amazonian phonology. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word unless the language is Goidelic (not the case here). Current game names contain q, f, l, d which are not Tupian and should be rejected.
